title: Integration discovery - Sunrise Retail
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
summary: Discovery call to understand Sunrise Retail's integration needs for conversational search and product Q&A. Main concerns: latency at peak traffic, data residency and encryption, SDK compatibility with LangChain/LlamaIndex stacks, and observability hooks for tracing. Next steps: share pricing and security pack, run a latency POC with sample prompts, SE to run integration guide with LangChain adapter, schedule follow-up in 1 week.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Aisha Patel (Redwood SE), Jonas Kim (Redwood SE), Evan Torres (CTO, Sunrise), Priya Shah (Lead ML Eng), Marco Diaz (Infra), Lena Wu (PM)

[00:00] Morgan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Morgan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. Aisha and Jonas are our SEs, they'll jump into technical stuff. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Evan Torres: Good, thanks. Excited to talk through integration options - we've been evaluating hosted and private for a couple of weeks.
[00:18] Priya Shah: Hi - quick background: we run recommendation and search systems across our web+mobile properties, peak concurrency during promos is about 4k rps, typical generation length ~80 tokens, but some chat flows go to 400 tokens.
[00:32] Aisha Patel: Great, that's helpful. Do you have an existing LLM gateway or are you looking to use Redwood as the primary proxy?
[00:40] Marco Diaz: We currently have an internal gateway that routes to OpenAI and a couple of open models on-prem, but it's mostly a simple proxy. We'd like to centralize routing, rate limiting and observability - so Redwood could be the gateway or integrate behind our proxy.
[00:55] Jonas Kim: Perfect - two common patterns: customers either send requests directly to Redwood hosted API or put Redwood behind their gateway (we support both). For Dedicated/Private customers we provide an endpoint that can sit in your VPC.
[01:05] Lena Wu: Quick Q on SDKs: our infra and ML stacks heavily use LangChain and LlamaIndex (we call it Llama index internally), is Redwood compatible?
[01:14] Aisha Patel: Yes - Redwood has official SDKs for Python/Node and first-class adapter integrations with LangChain and LlamaIndex. Small caveat: some community adapters have name mismatches in auto-detect, so we provide an adapter guide and a template repo.
[01:28] Priya Shah: When you say adapter guide, is that code we can drop in? We have a custom prompt runner so we want to avoid changing a lot.
[01:35] Aisha Patel: Absolutely - it's a small wrapper. We'll send a LangChain adapter example that shows how to swap the OpenAI client with Redwood, including streaming support and function/tool calling.
[01:45] Evan Torres: Streaming is key for us, most UX relies on incremental tokens. How's Redwood's streaming and socket support?
[01:52] Jonas Kim: Hosted API supports chunked HTTP streaming and websockets for long-lived connections. For Dedicated we can enable streaming via our regional endpoints; for Private (VPC/on-prem) streaming is supported but requires a lightweight agent in the customer network to handle connection upgrades.
[02:06] Marco Diaz: That agent - is it a binary? Any special networking rules?
[02:10] Aisha Patel: It's a small containerized agent that opens outbound connections to the control plane; inbound isn't required. We rely on mTLS between control plane and the agent and support customer-managed egress and proxying rules.
[02:22] Evan Torres: Ok good. Next: rate limiting. During promos traffic spikes 3-5x. We need per-route quotas, burst allowances, and predictable throttling behavior.
[02:32] Morgan Lee: We expose rate limits at the API key and route level. For Dedicated customers you can map customers to pools and set hard caps plus burst buckets. Our console also shows real-time quota usage and alerts.
[02:42] Priya Shah: Any soft-fail behavior we can use to degrade gracefully - e.g. fallback to embeddings-only or smaller model?
[02:48] Jonas Kim: Yes - routing policies allow fallback to a cheaper model variant or cached responses. You can configure automatic fallbacks based on latency percentiles or queue depth.
[02:57] Marco Diaz: Speaking of caching, does Redwood support prefix or KV cache sharing across nodes? We want cross-instance cache to reduce repeated context cost.
[03:06] Aisha Patel: We have prefix caching and a KV cache for token-level reuse; for Dedicated clusters the cache can be shared within the pool, and for Private you can integrate with your Redis or our managed cache. Sometimes transcriptions will say K V cache or K-V cache - basically it's a token KV.
[03:20] Priya Shah: Nice. On observability: we need traces, per-request token cost, latency percentiles, and per-route logs shipped to our ELK stack. What hooks do you provide?
[03:31] Jonas Kim: We emit structured logs with request id, model, tokens in/out, and latency. We also provide OpenTelemetry spans and a tracing hook you can enable. For security reasons we can omit prompt contents in logs or redact them at ingestion.
[03:45] Evan Torres: Redaction is a must. We also need audit logs for admin actions and an SSO integration.
[03:51] Morgan Lee: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, role-based access control, and audit logs retained per your plan. Security docs (SOC 2, ISO) are in our security pack; we'll share that.
[04:02] Lena Wu: Data residency - some of our EU customers must keep logs in-region. Can Dedicated or Private handle that?
[04:09] Aisha Patel: Yes - Dedicated can be provisioned in a specific region and Private gives you full control for in-region-only egress. Hosted offers regional endpoints but logs may be aggregated unless you pick the enterprise retention add-on.
[04:22] Priya Shah: About cost: do you have guidance on quantization or batching for cost reduction? Our use case is high-volume short responses for product Q&A.
[04:30] Jonas Kim: Redwood Optimize provides model and quantization recommendations. For short responses, aggressive batching and prefix caching yield big wins. We'll propose config suggestions based on your token distribution; SE can run model selection tests.
[04:45] Marco Diaz: What's the typical latency we should expect for a 80-token response under Dedicated with 4k rps?
[04:52] Aisha Patel: Depends on GPU profile and batching. With a latency-first config on A100-class or equivalent GPUs you can see p95s in the 120-180ms range for 80 tokens if batching is tuned and KV cache hit rate is high. If you prioritize throughput/cost you might see 250-400ms. We should run a benchmark with your actual prompts.
[05:10] Evan Torres: That sounds reasonable. For Private on-prem, any special SLA limitations?
[05:15] Morgan Lee: Private is more of a self-managed model - we offer an enterprise support bundle; SLA for control plane connectivity can be negotiated but the customer owns infra uptime. For Dedicated we provide SLA-backed latency windows.
[05:28] Lena Wu: Integration question: we use LangChain flows that do retrieval augmented generation with LlamaIndex. How transparent is the call path when using your SDK - will we still get per-step telemetry for the RAG retrieval calls?
[05:38] Jonas Kim: Yes, our SDK surfaces per-call metadata and you can attach your own trace ids. For RAG, if you call the Redwood embeddings and then the generative endpoint, you'll get telemetry for both. We'll include examples showing per-step trace propagation.
[05:52] Priya Shah: Do you support direct embeddings storage / vector DB integrations?
[05:56] Aisha Patel: We don't host a vector DB, but we have first-class connectors for Pinecone, Milvus, and we expose embeddings endpoints with deterministic outputs and metadata for easy ingestion.
[06:06] Evan Torres: SE question - our infra team wants to run an end-to-end POC: 1) drop in LangChain adapter, 2) run a small load test with 500 rps, 3) validate streaming and fallback behavior, 4) verify logs to our ELK. How long to set that up?
[06:20] Jonas Kim: We can get you sandbox API keys today. SE can help with the adapter and run the load test; typical setup is 2-3 days including tweaks. For Dedicated or Private POCs, provisioning the environment can add 1-2 weeks depending on region and capacity.
[06:34] Marco Diaz: Sandbox keys have quotas? We don't want to hit arbitrary limits during the test.
[06:38] Morgan Lee: Sandbox keys come with a test quota; for POC we can temporarily lift quotas for a controlled load test - we'll coordinate with infra to ensure fair-use and cost controls.
[06:48] Priya Shah: Any breaking changes we should be aware of in SDK versions? Our stack pins to a specific LangChain minor.
[06:55] Aisha Patel: We maintain semantic versioning for SDKs and provide migration notes. For LangChain adapters we try to support the last two major LangChain releases; if you pin an older one we can provide a compatibility shim.
[07:10] Lena Wu: Ok, security review - can you confirm KMS integration for customer-managed keys and whether Redwood can perform envelope encryption?
[07:18] Morgan Lee: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and HSM integrations for Dedicated and Private; envelope encryption is supported so primary keys are customer-controlled. We'll include the KMS architecture doc in the security pack.
[07:30] Evan Torres: About compliance, do you provide SOC 2 Type II and do you support contractual data processing addenda?
[07:36] Morgan Lee: We have SOC 2 Type II and standard DPAs for EU customers. For enterprise contracts we can negotiate addenda for data residency and retention.
[07:46] Priya Shah: One more nit: function calling in streaming - does Redwood support partial function responses and streaming function arguments?
[07:53] Jonas Kim: We support streaming JSON chunks and function/tool calling; partial payloads are possible but we recommend idempotent handlers on your side to tolerate re-ordered chunks. We'll share examples.
[08:06] Lena Wu: Are there known pitfalls when putting Redwood behind our existing gateway? We want to keep existing auth flow and a sidecar with token exchange.
[08:15] Aisha Patel: The main thing is preserving client idempotency keys and trace ids. You should pass through original headers or map them to Redwood request metadata. Also watch for double rate limiting - turn off gateway throttles for routes proxied to Redwood or map them carefully.
[08:30] Evan Torres: Pricing ask: can you share committed Dedicated pricing vs hosted burstable pricing?
[08:36] Morgan Lee: We'll share a pricing sheet. High level: hosted is usage-based with per-token pricing and optional reserved capacity credits. Dedicated is a capacity reservation model with monthly/annual commits; Private has licensing plus support fee. We'll include numbers in the follow-up.
[08:50] Priya Shah: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[08:55] Morgan Lee: Recap: we'll send security pack and pricing, Redwood SEs will share LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter examples and a demo repo, SE to provision sandbox keys and temporarily lift quotas for a 500 rps POC, schedule a technical deep-dive to run latency tests with your sample prompts, and we'll align on timeline for Dedicated/Private if POC looks good.
[09:18] Lena Wu: When can you run the POC?
[09:21] Jonas Kim: We can start the adapter integration tomorrow; the load test once we have sample prompts and a test harness - ideally early next week.
[09:28] Evan Torres: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[09:31] Morgan Lee: Thanks - we'll follow up with links and action items.

End of transcript.
